newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's Nat'l Coffee Fund not bankrupt -Ocampo.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's Nat'l Coffee Fund not bankrupt -Ocampo.

text.p: Reports of an imminent demise of Colombia's National Coffee Fund have been greatly exaggerated, Finance Minister Jose Antonio Ocampo said Saturday.

The fund has been hard hit by the recent strengthening of Colombia's peso currency, which erodes the domestic value of export revenues. Gabriel Rosas, head of the National Coffee Exporters' Association, said earlier this week that it was so heavily indebted that it could be forced to close down within three months.

But Ocampo, in a speech to the exporter association's annual assembly in this Caribbean port city, said there was no danger of the fund's collapse and no justification for "apocalyptic voices talking about its disappearance."

Contrary to recent press reports, which said the fund was saddled with a debt of about $800 million, Ocampo said it was expected to end the year with a deficit of no more than about $159 million and boasted a net worth of more than $1.68 billion.
"The fund has overcome many crises and it will overcome this one as well," he said.
The fund guarantees the purchase of crops from growers and has provided industry-wide stability for decades.
